scenarios.title: Explain exact snapshot drift
scenarios.summary: Distinguish useful drift from input errors without losing LF or changing a file.
scenarios.objective: Accept exactly LEFT RIGHT. Argument-count errors print Usage: compare LEFT RIGHT on stderr and exit2 first. Then both names must be one-line ASCII ^[a-z][a-z0-9.-]{0,11}$; otherwise Invalid files, exit2. Missing LEFT prints Missing left, exit2 before checking RIGHT; missing RIGHT prints Missing right, exit2. Compare the exact bounded UTF8/nonNUL contents, including every trailing LF. Same contents (including a file compared with itself) print Same, Left:LEFT and Right:RIGHT on three LF-terminated stdout lines and exit0. Different contents print Different and the same two name lines, exit1. Successful comparisons have empty stderr. Never change any file. These are this script's interface/status rules, not a full cmp utility.

cases.name: Equal minimum-name snapshots retain UTF8 whitespace CR and sentinel data
Whitespace-only data drift must remain different
A final LF alone is meaningful drift
Multiple final LFs are not normalized
Empty text differs from an empty physical line
Thirteen-character filename refused despite existing inputs
The same supplied file may be compared with itself
Missing left takes priority
Missing right is not reported as ordinary drift
Argument error precedes file validation
Trailing LF inside a filename is refused
Maximum mixed-class names and later-line drift

solution:
valid_name() {
  case "$1" in
    *'
'*) return 1 ;;
  esac
  printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep -Eq -- '^[a-z][a-z0-9.-]{0,11}$'
}
snapshot() {
  if cat -- "$1"; then printf '.'; else return 2; fi
}
same_files() {
  left_value=$(snapshot "$1")
  capture_status=$?
  if test "$capture_status" -ne 0; then return 2; fi
  right_value=$(snapshot "$2")
  capture_status=$?
  if test "$capture_status" -ne 0; then return 2; fi
  test "$left_value" = "$right_value"
}
if test "$#" -ne 2; then printf 'Usage: compare LEFT RIGHT\n' >&2; exit 2; fi
if valid_name "$1" && valid_name "$2"; then :; else printf 'Invalid files\n' >&2; exit 2; fi
if test -f "$1"; then :; else printf 'Missing left\n' >&2; exit 2; fi
if test -f "$2"; then :; else printf 'Missing right\n' >&2; exit 2; fi
if same_files "$1" "$2"; then
  printf 'Same\nLeft:%s\nRight:%s\n' "$1" "$2"
  exit 0
else
  comparison_status=$?
  if test "$comparison_status" -ne 1; then printf 'Cannot compare\n' >&2; exit 2; fi
  printf 'Different\nLeft:%s\nRight:%s\n' "$1" "$2"
  exit 1
fi
scenarios.explanation: Preflight the interface and required files. Capture after a checked read with a fixed nonLF suffix; compare the whole values or remove that exact suffix with the reviewed literal form. Preserve all bytes. For rollout, validate every row and every path before writing, retain changed old-current data independently and leave unchanged rollback data intact. Staged and repeated-read approaches are both valid under disjoint immutable inputs. This is final-state/preflight behavior; operation order, atomic rename, races and Stop rollback are not graded.
hints: A normal capture can erase the only difference: trailing LF. Preserve that boundary before comparing.
Separate input trouble from useful same/different information; save helper status before another command replaces it.
Validate both input names and existence first. Compare the complete preserved values, keep both files unchanged, and return1 only for real drift.

teaching.prerequisite_note: First finish the earlier quoted capture, IFS read, functions/status, arrays, loop and literal-interface lessons. This unit teaches a lossless sentinel comparison before using it in a rollout. No wc, cmp, diff, trap or host utility is available.

concepts.title: Compare contents, not names or first lines
concepts.text: Two different filenames may hold identical data. A same/different decision uses every byte in this simulator's bounded valid UTF8 text, including blank lines, CR, backslashes and trailing LF. Binary and NUL files are outside this model.

concepts.title: Why the same suffix preserves trailing LF
concepts.text: Command capture removes all final LF bytes. Append one fixed nonLF marker inside each capture, after cat succeeds, so the final character is not LF. Compare the complete marked values. The same suffix is safe even when that marker occurs in the data; it is not written into files.

concepts.title: A nonzero result can be useful information
concepts.text: The comparison helper returns0 for equal,1 for different,2 for input trouble. Save $? immediately if you need to distinguish them. A later successful printf must not conceal a failed read. Use explicit if/else; no errexit or trap is assumed.

concepts.title: Read preserves a final fragment differently
concepts.text: IFS= read -r preserves edge spaces and backslashes, removes one consumed LF, and reports0 only when it found LF. A nonempty last fragment is still assigned with status1; empty EOF assigns empty/status1. A read-based alternative must put LF back only for successful complete-line reads.

concepts.title: Decide the whole plan before opening outputs
concepts.text: Validate the interface, every row, required inputs and all path conflicts before changing a file. A changed job needs an independent old-current rollback. An unchanged job preserves the existing rollback or its absence. Protected input and keep.txt must remain intact.

concepts.title: What this preflight promise does not mean
concepts.text: A predictable validation refusal preserves every file. Ordinary writes are not atomic rename or a lock: Stop or a resource failure during writing is not promised to roll back earlier work. Completion checks current outcomes, not a transcript count or required command spelling.

scenarios.simplifications: Only bounded valid UTF8/nonNUL flat virtual text files; no host execution, arbitrary binary cmp conformance, file metadata or modification counters. Same/different is exact text-byte equality, not Unicode normalization. No directories, links, tempfiles, rename, locking, traps, real clock, races or guaranteed Stop/resource rollback. Predictable preflight refusals preserve every file. Examples and drafts are isolated.
scenarios.retry_guidance: Read the selected outcome and complete file differences. Check LF boundaries and error priority before changing publication logic; use a separate example to investigate.

scenarios.title: Review and apply a protected rollout
scenarios.summary: Preflight every job, update only changed targets and preserve independent rollback data.
scenarios.objective: Accept exactly MODE PLAN REPORT, MODE preview or apply; wrong interface/mode prints Usage: rollout preview-or-apply PLAN REPORT and exit2 before file checks. PLAN/REPORT use one-line ASCII ^[a-z][a-z0-9.-]{0,11}$, must differ and neither may be keep.txt; otherwise Invalid files, exit2. A missing PLAN prints Missing plan, exit2. PLAN has0–8 physical records; the last need not end with LF. Every row is exactly desired|current|rollback with the same three name grammars. On each row, first reject row9 as too many jobs, then malformed job, then conflicting paths, then missing desired, then missing current. All three paths across ALL rows must be unique and may not equal PLAN, REPORT or protected keep.txt. Errors print Line N: REASON on stderr and exit2, preserving every file. Compare each pair exactly. A same row leaves current AND its existing/absent rollback untouched. A changed apply row sets rollback to the old current bytes and current to desired bytes. Every desired file, PLAN, keep.txt and unrelated file remain unchanged. Build row lines same|current or change|current in original order, followed by Changes:N and Unchanged:M; every line ends LF. Preview prints Preview then those report lines on stdout, writes no files, and exits0. Apply writes those report lines to REPORT and prints Applied:N and Unchanged:M on stdout, exits0. Success stderr is empty. Empty plans are valid. Preflight covers the complete plan before ANY write. Final state and predictable-refusal preservation are graded; atomicity, write chronology and Stop/resource rollback are not.

solution:
valid_name() {
  case "$1" in
    *'
'*) return 1 ;;
  esac
  printf '%s\n' "$1" | grep -Eq -- '^[a-z][a-z0-9.-]{0,11}$'
}
snapshot() {
  if cat -- "$1"; then printf '.'; else return 2; fi
}
same_files() {
  left_value=$(snapshot "$1")
  capture_status=$?
  if test "$capture_status" -ne 0; then return 2; fi
  right_value=$(snapshot "$2")
  capture_status=$?
  if test "$capture_status" -ne 0; then return 2; fi
  test "$left_value" = "$right_value"
}
usage() { printf 'Usage: rollout preview-or-apply PLAN REPORT\n' >&2; exit 2; }
bad_line() { printf 'Line %s: %s\n' "$number" "$1" >&2; exit 2; }
if test "$#" -ne 3; then usage; fi
mode=$1
plan_file=$2
report_file=$3
case "$mode" in preview|apply) : ;; *) usage ;; esac
if valid_name "$plan_file" && valid_name "$report_file"; then :; else printf 'Invalid files\n' >&2; exit 2; fi
if test "$plan_file" = "$report_file" || test "$plan_file" = keep.txt || test "$report_file" = keep.txt; then
  printf 'Invalid files\n' >&2
  exit 2
fi
if test -f "$plan_file"; then :; else printf 'Missing plan\n' >&2; exit 2; fi
number=0
changed=0
unchanged=0
report_text=''
staged=()
seen="|$plan_file|$report_file|keep.txt|"
while IFS= read -r line || test -n "$line"; do
  number=$((number+1))
  if test "$number" -gt 8; then bad_line 'too many jobs'; fi
  if printf '%s\n' "$line" | grep -Eq -- '^[a-z][a-z0-9.-]{0,11}[|][a-z][a-z0-9.-]{0,11}[|][a-z][a-z0-9.-]{0,11}$'; then :; else bad_line 'malformed job'; fi
  desired=$(printf '%s\n' "$line" | cut -d '|' -f 1)
  current=$(printf '%s\n' "$line" | cut -d '|' -f 2)
  rollback=$(printf '%s\n' "$line" | cut -d '|' -f 3)
  for name in "$desired" "$current" "$rollback"; do
    case "$seen" in *"|$name|"*) bad_line 'conflicting paths' ;; esac
    seen=$seen$name'|'
  done
  if test -f "$desired"; then :; else bad_line 'missing desired'; fi
  if test -f "$current"; then :; else bad_line 'missing current'; fi
  if same_files "$desired" "$current"; then
    decision=same
    unchanged=$((unchanged+1))
  else
    comparison_status=$?
    if test "$comparison_status" -ne 1; then bad_line 'cannot compare'; fi
    decision=change
    changed=$((changed+1))
  fi
  staged=( "${staged[@]}" "$decision|$desired|$current|$rollback" )
  report_text=$report_text$decision'|'$current'
'
done < "$plan_file"
report_text=$report_text'Changes:'$changed'
Unchanged:'$unchanged'
'
if test "$mode" = preview; then printf 'Preview\n%s' "$report_text"; exit 0; fi
for job in "${staged[@]}"; do
  decision=$(printf '%s\n' "$job" | cut -d '|' -f 1)
  desired=$(printf '%s\n' "$job" | cut -d '|' -f 2)
  current=$(printf '%s\n' "$job" | cut -d '|' -f 3)
  rollback=$(printf '%s\n' "$job" | cut -d '|' -f 4)
  if test "$decision" = change; then
    cat -- "$current" > "$rollback"
    cat -- "$desired" > "$current"
  fi
done
printf '%s' "$report_text" > "$report_file"
printf 'Applied:%s\nUnchanged:%s\n' "$changed" "$unchanged"
exit 0
